problem_markdown: Define $u_0=2$, $u_1=5/2$, and $u_{n+1}=u_n(u_{n-1}^2-2)-u_1$ for $n\ge1$. Show that $\lfloor u_n\rfloor=2^{(2^n-(-1)^n)/3}$ for every $n\ge1$.
solutions_markdown:
Put $e_n=(2^n-(-1)^n)/3$, a nonnegative integer, and $v_n=2^{e_n}+2^{-e_n}$. Then $v_0=2,v_1=5/2$. The identities
$$e_n+2e_{n-1}=e_{n+1},\qquad e_n-2e_{n-1}=(-1)^{n-1}$$
show, by multiplying the two reciprocal-power pairs, that
$$v_n(v_{n-1}^2-2)=v_{n+1}+2+\tfrac12.$$
Thus $v_n$ obeys the defining recurrence, and induction gives $u_n=v_n$. For $n\ge1$, $e_n\ge1$, so $2^{e_n}$ is an integer and $0<2^{-e_n}<1$. Taking floors proves the formula.
